message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <ZONE> with your preferred zone)
ZONENAME=<ZONE>

# 2. Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --zone=$ZONENAME \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --boot-disk-size=200GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional init script
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU (`count=1`). |
| `--boot-disk-size` | SSD size for OS + local storage. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at boot (e.g., install drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or different CPU/RAM, change `count=` and `--machine-type`.  
> **Tip:** To automatically install the NVIDIA driver, add a `startup.sh` like:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": "200",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "labels": { "purpose": "demo-gpu" }
}
```

Send it via:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances"
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your actual values.

---

### Quick Checklist

- ✅ **GPU quota** – Ensure you have an RTX A6000 quota in the selected zone.  
- ✅ **Billing enabled** – GPU instances incur extra charges.  
- ✅ **Driver installation** – Either use the `startup.sh` approach or manually SSH into the VM after creation and run `sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall`.  

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or network settings to match your workload!
